source: scripts/fetch_latest_videos.py + scripts/analyze_past_performance.py, run 2026-11-21 (compared with the 2026-11-17 snapshot)
headline: Two pillars work, and YouTube's own AI agrees: (1) practical, cost-saving dev tooling, where the cheap-model Shorts get about 190 views each, 4× your other recent Shorts; and (2) grounded long-form career/industry takes with a data angle (Elon 348, Delivery Pilot 135). What doesn't work is mindset Shorts and narrow commentary.

findings.title: Cheap-model tool Shorts are your best format right now
findings.detail: 'Make DeepSeek work like a frontier model in Kilo CLI' (195) and 'Don't Pay $200: Give Your Cheap AI Model Glasses' (185) are the two most-watched uploads of the comeback. Your other 6 recent Shorts average about 50 views, and the mindset ones get 12–23.

findings.title: Timely Claude fix videos are growing fastest
findings.detail: 'Claude Whiteboards Missing?' gained +17 views in 4 days, more than any other video. Its 'X is missing, here's the fix' title is something people actually type into search.

findings.title: The Interview Overlay video is your fastest grower
findings.detail: It went from 15 views (Studio export, 18 Nov) to 76 (21 Nov): +61 in 3 days, about 20 a day, the best rate on the channel. Your all-time #1 (LinkedIn job hunt AI, 552) and the CV and cover-letter videos follow the same pattern: an AI tool built for a job-seeker outcome.

findings.title: Mindset Shorts and narrow commentary get passed over
findings.detail: 'Rider, Driver or Pilot?' (12), 'AI Has No Values. You Do.' (23), 'Stuck in Red Tape?' (10). Big-picture takes do work as long-form with a data-backed, contrarian hook ('Elon Says Work Is Ending. The Data Says Otherwise.' 348; 'Become a Delivery Pilot' 135), but not as 45-second Shorts or on niche angles.

findings.title: The junior-dev Delivery Pilot video is too new to judge
findings.detail: It's YouTube AI's idea #2, already made: first published as 'Junior Developer Jobs Aren't Dead. They're Becoming Delivery Pilots (2027)' (15 views), retitled 'The UK Junior Dev Crash Is a J-Curve' (18 views after about a day). The retitle narrowed it to the UK; YouTube's framing (Delivery Pilot roles in 2027) is broader. Judge it at 7 days against 'Become a Delivery Pilot' (about 11 views/day).

findings.title: Two uploads on the same day split the audience
findings.detail: On Nov 10, 11 and 21 you published two videos each day. Each time, one of the pair underperformed. A small channel gets one push from YouTube per upload.

findings.title: Your back catalogue is flat
findings.detail: Almost every video older than 2 months gained 0 views in 4 days. Old videos are getting no search traffic, so new uploads and Shorts are doing all the work.

findings.title: We only see view counts
findings.detail: The subscriber count (725) is hardcoded in analyze_past_performance.py and has not been re-measured. The 18 Nov Studio export has views and comments, but no CTR, retention or subscribers-per-video. Thumbnail A/B tests are still running on the 3 newest long videos. The scraper only sees about the newest 30 long videos, so older ones (e.g. 'CV as Code', 304 views) drop out of the totals. YOUTUBE_API_KEY is not set, so scripts/pull_youtube_stats.py could not run.

actions.title: Turn the cheap-model Shorts into a series
actions.detail: Film 3 more in the same shape: '[cheap model] + [one tool trick] = frontier results'. Ideas: Qwen/GLM in Kilo Code, MCP tools for a cheap model, a context-file trick that cuts tokens. Same hook structure: 'Don't pay $X…'.

actions.title: Make the parent long-form for that series
actions.detail: Make 'Frontier-level AI coding for under $10/month (full setup)' next Wednesday's video. Link it from all the cheap-model Shorts and pin it. That turns Short viewers into watch time.

actions.title: Cut Shorts from the two videos that are moving
actions.detail: Pull 2 Shorts from the Interview Overlay video (the live coaching moment, and the setup in 45s) and 1 from Claude Whiteboards (the fix). Repurpose what is already working before making something new.

actions.title: One upload per day, maximum
actions.detail: Never publish two videos on the same day. Space Shorts at least 24h apart and keep long-form on Wednesday so each upload gets its own push.

actions.title: Use search-style titles for timely topics
actions.detail: When Claude, Kilo or DeepSeek ships something, publish within 48h with a problem-first title ('X missing?', 'X not working?', 'X vs Y for $0'). This is the only thing growing without help.

actions.title: Put Delivery Pilot inside the tool videos
actions.detail: Stop making standalone mindset Shorts. Use the Pilot framing as the closing line of a practical video, where it lands with people who already got value.

actions.title: Measure what matters
actions.detail: Make the analysis script read the live subscriber count and keep a dated snapshot each run so growth is tracked automatically. Export CTR and retention from YouTube Studio into data/studio/ so this page can rank by retention, not just views.

videoReviews.title: The UK Junior Dev Crash Is a J-Curve (And Here's the Upswing)
videoReviews.made: After the YouTube Studio AI analysis (idea #2: junior dev jobs shifting to Delivery Pilot roles in 2027)
videoReviews.summary: Following YouTube's advice was the right call. This is your best-researched career take: a data-led, contrarian hook, which is the same shape as 'Elon Says Work Is Ending. The Data Says Otherwise.' (348). The problem is packaging. The title sells a UK economics story (J-curve), the description sells Rider/Driver/Pilot and COBALTS, and the most useful part for the viewer, the 90-day plan, doesn't start until 8:35. Early engagement is healthy: 2 likes on 19 views (about 10%). Fix the packaging before judging the views.
strengths: Strong opening hook: 'UK entry-level roles are down by about half. So why am I more optimistic than ever?' That's a contrarian claim backed by data in the first 5 seconds.

Credible sources (SignalFire, a Harvard study of 62M workers, Brynjolfsson's productivity J-curve, the Linux Foundation, IBM, Cognizant, Cloudflare) and honest caveats: 'a model, not a promise', interest rates, and the IBM disclosure.
A clear idea at the core: 'CI became AI's job. Delivery became yours.'
It ends with something to do: a 90-day plan in three legs, plus a free course and Skool call to action.
issues: The title, description and video promise different things. The title is about the UK and the J-curve, the description is about Rider/Driver/Pilot and COBALTS, and the video covers both plus a 90-day plan. YouTube and searchers can't tell what the video is for.
'UK' narrows it, but the evidence is global (SignalFire, US Harvard data, Europe). 'J-curve' is economists' language that few people search for.

The thumbnail says 'THE J-CURVE −50%'. The −50% works as a hook, but 'J-curve' tells a scrolling developer nothing about what's in it for them. Try '−50%' with 'DELIVERY PILOT', or 'JUNIOR DEVS: 90-DAY PLAN'.

There are too many frameworks for 10 minutes: J-curve, CI checklist, Rider/Driver/Pilot, the pilot's 4 duties, everyone moving up a seat, COBALTS, a day in the life, and the 90-day plan. The concrete takeaway arrives at 8:35.
No chapters. With 14 distinct sections, chapters would help retention and give each section its own search entry.
Background music runs under the voice the whole way through. Check that the music sits low enough to keep the voice clear.
The 'Rider, Driver or Pilot?' Short went out the same day, so the two competed instead of the Short sending people to the long video.

fixes.title: Retitle to match the promise and YouTube's framing
fixes.detail: Try: 'Junior Dev Jobs Are Down 50%. Here's How to Become a Delivery Pilot in 90 Days (2027)', or go back to the original 'Junior Developer Jobs Aren't Dead. They're Becoming Delivery Pilots (2027)'. Keep the data hook, add the outcome, and drop 'UK' and 'J-curve'.

fixes.title: Rewrite the first two lines of the description
fixes.detail: Search results show only these lines, so they should repeat the title's promise: the data, why it's an upswing, and the 90-day plan. Move Rider/Driver/Pilot and COBALTS lower down.

fixes.title: Pin a comment with the 90-day plan
fixes.detail: Weeks 1–4: write specs. Weeks 5–8: build one agent and publish its logs. Weeks 9–12: get certified (CCAF). Add the Skool link. It puts the payoff at the top for people who skip ahead.

fixes.title: Cut 3 Shorts that send viewers here, on separate days
fixes.detail: (1) 'CI became AI's job. Delivery became yours.' (2:22–3:50) (2) 'If you stop hiring juniors, you stop making seniors.' (6:45–7:15) (3) The 90-day flight plan (8:35–9:40). Each one links to this video.

fixes.title: Next time: one framework per video
fixes.detail: Rider/Driver/Pilot plus COBALTS plus the 90-day plan is enough for three videos. Keeping one per video also gives you more videos for your strongest pillar.

videoReviews.judgeOn: 2026-11-28: after 7 days, compare views/day with 'Become a Delivery Pilot' (about 11 views/day). If it's lower after the retitle, the topic is fine and the packaging needs another pass.
